questions.prompt: What is the intent of the Interpreter pattern?

options.text: Define a representation for a language's grammar plus an interpreter that uses it to interpret sentences
Add operations to an object structure without changing its classes
Ensure a class has one instance
Convert one interface into another

questions.explanation: Interpreter maps grammar rules to classes that evaluate themselves. Adding operations without changing classes = Visitor; one instance = Singleton; converting = Adapter.

questions.prompt: What is the intent of the Visitor pattern?

options.text: Define a new operation over an object structure without changing the element classes
Interpret sentences of a small language
Share intrinsic state across many objects
Provide a simplified interface to a subsystem

questions.explanation: Visitor externalizes operations so elements needn't change. Interpreting = Interpreter; sharing state = Flyweight; simplifying = Facade.

questions.prompt: What is 'double dispatch', which Visitor relies on?

options.text: Selecting behavior based on two types — the element and the visitor
Calling a method twice for safety
Sending the same event to two subjects
Cloning an object two levels deep

questions.explanation: element.accept(visitor) dispatches on the element, then visitor.visitConcrete(this) dispatches on the visitor — two types decide the behavior.

questions.prompt: What is the 'expression problem' as it applies to Visitor?

options.text: Visitor makes adding new operations easy but adding new element types hard (every visitor must change)
Visitors cannot evaluate math expressions
Interpreters can't handle variables
Double dispatch is impossible in TypeScript

questions.explanation: New operation = new visitor (easy); new element type = a new visit method in every visitor (hard).

questions.prompt: When is Interpreter usually the WRONG choice?

options.text: For anything beyond a small, stable grammar — a real language needs a proper parser
For evaluating a tiny boolean filter language
For a simple arithmetic expression
For a small configuration DSL

questions.explanation: A class-per-rule design doesn't scale to complex languages; use a parser or parser generator instead.

options.text: Many operations over a stable set of element types
Frequent addition of new element types
Exactly one operation, forever
A single global instance

questions.explanation: Visitor pays off when operations multiply but element types stay stable; changing types often is where it hurts.
